  c : ℝ

      ∀(a ε T allowance κplain ν C height q : ℝ) (i : ℕ),
      1<U → 51/100<a → 2*a-1≤3/4 → 0≤ε → ε≤1/1000 →
      7/10≤κplain → κplain≤3/4 → 0<ν → 0≤C → 0≤height →
      2*Real.pi*allowance+(3*i:ℕ)*T≤height →
      ∀{Label Slot : Type} [Fintype Label] (B : Batch M H Label Slot U a ε (cutoff (2*a-1) (q/(2*a-1)) κplain) T allowance i),

        (Fintype.card B.Bin:ℝ)*

statement:
### B2.1. The completed family and fixed conventions

Write \(\mathcal O=\mathbb Z[\omega]\), \(\lambda=1+2\omega\), \(q_a=|a|^2\), and \(\alpha(a)=a/|a|\). Throughout \(Z\ge2\). Ideals prime to \(\lambda\) are represented by their unique primary generators \(a\equiv1\pmod3\). Let \(S\) be a fixed finite set containing the primes above \(6\); “good” means prime to \(S\). We use the sextic characters and normalized Gauss coefficients of the arithmetic section. Every integer power of a residue character is zero on a nonunit, including exponent zero:
\[
\chi_p(A)^0=1_{p\nmid A}.
\tag{B2.1}
\]
In particular, exponent reduction modulo six never removes a coprimality condition.

Fix a finite family of finite-ray characters \(\nu\), with conductors supported on \(S\), extended by zero outside the primary ideals coprime to \(S\). A squarefree good label \(f\) and a squarefree puncture radical \(r_\rho\) may vary between invocations. Within a row norm they are fixed, and
\[
\rho(A)=1_{(A,r_\rho)=1},\qquad
\Psi_k(A)=\nu(A)\rho(A)\chi_A(k)\chi_A(f)^4.
\tag{B2.2}
\]
The puncture may depend on previously frozen outer labels; it is independent of the current row and, when \(f\) is averaged later, of that averaging variable.

For a fixed number of pairwise disjoint prime lists \(\mathcal P_i\), with \(q_p\asymp Z^{z_i}\) on the \(i\)-th list and \(|a_i(p)|\le1\), put
\[
d(A)=\sum_{(p_i)\in\prod_i\mathcal P_i}
       \prod_i a_i(p_i)\,1_{\prod_i p_i\mid A},
\qquad z=\sum_i z_i.
\tag{B2.3}
\]
The completed sum at length \(X\) is
\[
\mathcal T_d(X;k;V)=
\sum_{\substack{n\ {\rm sf},\,b\\ (nb,S)=1}}
\frac{\overline{\alpha(n)}\gamma_2(n)\Psi_k(n)\,
      \overline{\alpha(b)}^{\,3}\Psi_k(b)^3}
     {\sqrt{q_n}\,q_b}\,
d(nb^3)V(q_nq_b^3/X).
\tag{B2.4}
\]
The two primal ideals may share primes. An annular smooth test is allowed, as is any test rapidly decreasing with all Euler derivatives at both endpoints. The factor \(y^{1/2}\) converting an annular uncompleted sum to (B2.4) is included in \(V\).

We also allow one common smooth profile in the completed norm and the individual marked-prime norms, supported in fixed logarithmic boxes in the latter variables: expand (B2.3) in (B2.4), then put this profile inside the tuple sum. Logarithmic Fourier inversion in those variables reduces it to (B2.4), with an absolutely integrable common family of tests \(V\). Bounds below depend on finitely many weighted Euler seminorms of that profile. They are uniform in the prime lists, their bounded coefficients, \(k,f,r_\rho\), and all norm labels whose logarithms to base \(Z\) lie in fixed bounded ranges. Imaginary norm powers incur only a fixed polynomial in their heights. Product form in (B2.3) is required when slots are assigned to extracted factors; after that assignment, the remaining tuple coefficient may be any bounded function independent of the row and dual indices.

The only imported analytic results are the unconditional theta expansions in Dunn–Radziwiłł [DR, §5 and Appendix A], Goldmakher–Louvel’s quadratic Hecke large sieve [GL, Definition 1 and Theorem 1.1], and Heath-Brown’s cubic large sieve [HB, Theorem 2]. All moving-conductor and marked-index reductions are proved below.
title: B2.1. The completed family and fixed conventions

statement:
## Abstract

We prove that the Riemann zeta function, every Dirichlet \(L\)-function, and every finite-order Hecke \(L\)-function over \(\mathbf Q(\sqrt{-3})\) have no zero in \(\Re s>29/33\), with principal poles at one allowed. A cubic-theta probe exposes a reciprocal \(L\)-function after Poisson summation. One compensating prime strengthens its principal signal, while two polynomial witnesses detected at the same zero control the remaining rows. The decisive exponent comparison is an exact nonnegative square. We prove the required polynomial moments, reflection estimates, and finite arithmetic identities from classical theta formulas and large sieves.
title: Abstract

statement:
#### B2.4.2. Quadratic reduction for a squarefree index times a cube

Let \(k\) be squarefree good with \(q_k\ll K\), \(n\) squarefree primary with \(q_n\asymp N\), and \(b\) primary with \(q_b\asymp B\). The dual \(n,b\) may contain primes of \(S\) other than \(\lambda\). Let \(\beta(n,b)\) be arbitrary, independent of \(k\); fixed support restrictions are allowed.

Write uniquely
\[
b=gt^2,\qquad c=(n,g),\qquad n=cm,\qquad g=ch,
\]
where \(g\) is squarefree and \(c,m,h\) are pairwise coprime squarefree ideals. There is no restriction \((g,t)=1\). On dyads \(q_c\asymp C,\ q_g\asymp G,\ q_t\asymp T\), we have \(B\asymp GT^2\) and the exact identity
\[
\chi_k(nb)^3=\chi_k(mh)^3\,1_{(k,ct)=1}.
\tag{B2.26}
\]
Cauchy in \(t\) costs \(O(T)\). Fix \(t\), retain \((k,t)=1\) as a row restriction, and expand the entire remaining mask:
\(1_{(k,c)=1}=\sum_{r\mid(k,c)}\mu(r)\).
Rowwise divisor Cauchy costs \((KNB)^\epsilon\). For fixed \(r\), write \(k=rk'\), \(c=rc'\). Squarefreeness gives fixed restrictions \((k',r)=(c',r)=1\), and terms with \((r,t)>1\) vanish. There is no remaining \((k',c')\)-mask in an individual \(r\)-summand.

The factor \(\chi_r(mh)^3\) is column-only. Split the finitely many squarefree \(S\)-parts of \(m,h\), whose characters are row scalars. Their good product \(j=m_{\rm good}h_{\rm good}\) is squarefree with norm \(O(NG/C^2)\). Group by \(j\), use (B2.24) with row length \(K/q_r\), then Cauchy over the divisor-bounded factorizations of \(j\) and the \(O(C/q_r)\) choices of \(c'\). If \(\mathcal D_r(t)\) retains all original conditions on \((c',m,h)\), the resulting bound is
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_{C,G,T}(\beta)
\ll_\epsilon (KNB)^\epsilon T
\sum_{q_t\asymp T}
\sum_{\substack{r\ {\rm sf,good}\\q_r\ll\min(K,C)}}
\left(\frac K{q_r}+\frac{NG}{C^2}\right)\frac C{q_r}
\sum_{(c',m,h)\in\mathcal D_r(t)}
|\beta(rc'm,rc'ht^2)|^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{B2.27}
\]
This more precise positive bound will preserve the tuple independence in the next step. In particular, for \(|\beta|\le1\), the triple count is \(O(NG/(q_rC))\). In a dyad \(q_r\asymp r_0\), counting its \(O(r_0)\) divisors and the \(O(T)\) values of \(t\) gives
\[
\ll (KNB)^\epsilon\frac{NB}{r_0}
\left(\frac K{r_0}+\frac{NG}{C^2}\right)
\ll(KNB)^\epsilon NB(K+NB).
\]
Triangle inequality over the logarithmically many \(C,G,T\)-dyads proves
\[
\sum_k\left|\sum_{n,b}\beta(n,b)\chi_k(nb)^3\right|^2
\ll_\epsilon(KNB)^\epsilon(K+NB)NB.
\tag{B2.28}
\]
Subunit quotient ranges are empty; bounded ranges, including the unit ideal, are covered by fixed comparison constants.
title: B2.4.2. Quadratic reduction for a squarefree index times a cube

statement:
### Section 8: Row counts

The orientation paragraph is correct: the whole witness product is conjugated when needed, not merely its character notation. The resulting prime coefficients remain fixed independently of the row.

The inverse and plain capacities are applied with their proper hypotheses. The inverse capacity is decremented by a fixed positive amount, so the argument does not take an unjustified limit of estimates requiring strict inequalities.

The passage from \(\kappa_0\) to
\[
\kappa=2B-1
\]
is explicitly paid for. The bound
\[
\frac{30}{169}\Delta<\frac{\Delta}{4}
\]
is correct.

The crucial logical point is that the plain lemma’s premise is discharged by the definition of this \(\kappa\):
\[
B=\frac{1+\kappa}{2}.
\]
Its use is therefore not a conditional assumption about an independently conjectured zero-free region.

The cases \(\delta\le5/6\), \(\delta\ge5/6\), the unselected alternative, and the floor are separately handled.
title: Section 8: Row counts

statement:
# Source notices

Copyright 2026 Hailey Collet. New manuscript and formalization material are
licensed under Apache-2.0. See `LICENSE` and `PROVENANCE.md`.

The vendored `formalization/OAI/` source is the exact import closure from
[OpenAI/math](https://github.com/openai/math) at
`fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb`. It retains its upstream authorship
and Apache-2.0 license. The source inventory records each included module.
The new proof uses that development's original 7/8 nonvanishing theorem as
a weaker initialization, as well as its analytic and arithmetic foundations.

The `Cycle25` development adapts the numerator inversion, conductor allocation,
coefficient estimates and contour assembly of Akash Levy's
[weighted-numerator proof](https://github.com/akashlevy/QuasiRiemannTracker/tree/2fd60c0926b66ea18d7436f5ed55250fd006ab5d/proofs/akashlevy-20261009-weighted-numerator),
revision `2fd60c0926b66ea18d7436f5ed55250fd006ab5d`, and generalizes the moment,
counting and geometric estimates to the quartic endpoint. That source's
license and notice are retained in `licenses/`; its notice describes the
original upstream package. Its previous final nonvanishing theorem is not
used to establish the new endpoint.

The three `ZetaZeroFree/Analytic/Moments/` modules are reused from Hailey
Collet's [4/33 formalization](https://github.com/GTimG/QuasiRiemannTracker/pull/8).
They reorganize and adapt intermediate OpenAI proofs to establish an
unconditional moving-radical moment. The earlier 4/33 nonvanishing theorem
is not a dependency of this submission.

Mathlib, PrimeNumberTheoremAnd, rellich-kondrachov and the remaining Lake
dependencies retain their own authorship and licenses. Their exact revisions
and the required compatibility patches are recorded with the build recipe.
The patches retain the original licenses; only files needed by this proof's
import closure are included.

Lean, Comparator, NanoDa, con-ron, lean4export and the Palomar verification
helpers are used under their respective licenses. Their binaries are not
redistributed. No upstream project or maintainer endorsement is implied.

statement:
\begin{lemma}[Canonical marked estimate]\label{lem:canonical-moment}
Fix bounded nonnegative ranges for \(M,N,V,z_0\), a bound for the number
of slots, and \(c_*>0\).  Let \(f\) range over squarefree ideals outside
\(S\) with \(q_f\asymp Z^V\).  Let \(w\) be a nonnegative function of
\(f\) alone satisfying \(w(f)\le C d_{\mathcal O}(f)^C\) for one fixed
\(C\ge1\).  Neither \(C\) nor the choice of \(w\) depends on \(Z\),
the current rows, or any other averaged variable.  The implied constant
below may depend on \(C\), but is uniform over all \(w\) satisfying this
fixed bound.  Let \(\nu\) be a fixed
multiplicative finite ray character whose full zero-extended defining
modulus has prime support in \(S\), and let
\(\rho(n)=1_{(n,\mathfrak r_\rho)=1}\) be a fixed puncture.  Both are
independent of \(k,f\).  Let \(\mathfrak d\) have the product form in
Equation~\eqref{own:mark-definition}, with disjoint fixed prime lists of total
length at most \(z_0\) and bounded coefficients independent of \(k,f\).
No other row-dependent column coefficient or puncture is allowed.
There is no additional residual coefficient \(b(n)\), even one
independent of \(k,f\): arbitrary bounded weights are permitted only
as the stated product of individual prime-slot coefficients.

Put \(F_0=N+V\).  Suppose
\begin{equation}\label{eq:invariant}
 \begin{gathered}
 q_{\mathfrak r_\rho}\le Z^{F_0-M-z_0-c_*},\\
 3M+6z_0+c_*\le4F_0.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
For every smooth annular \(W\) and every \(\epsilon>0\), define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:canonical-energy}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal E={}&Z^{-V}\sum_f w(f)
 \sum_{\substack{k\in\mathcal O\\0<q_k\ll Z^M}}
 \Biggl|Z^{-N/2}\sum_{n\ {\rm sf}}
 \bar\alpha(n)\gamma_2(n)\nu(n)\rho(n)\\
 &\hspace{24mm}\times
 \chi_n(k)\chi_n(f)^4\mathfrak d(n)W(q_n/Z^N)\Biggr|^2.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Then \(\mathcal E\ll Z^{F_0+\epsilon}\).  The constant is uniform in
the moving moduli and the frozen outer ideals within the stated ranges.
It depends on finitely many smooth seminorms and has a fixed polynomial
dependence on separated norm-twist heights.  The same conclusion holds
for all subcollections of the slots with the original cap \(z_0\),
including the empty collection.
\end{lemma}
title: lem:canonical-moment

statement:
#### Retained nonprincipal rows

Fix \(d_{\min}=1/200\) and a sufficiently small positive extension
\(\zeta_0\). For \(U=Z^d\), with
\(d_{\min}\le d\le h+\zeta_0\), partition nonprincipal rows into
the buffered bins of §B0.2.

For each bin move \(z\) to \(z_0=17/50\), keeping \(s=2,w=3\).
Next move \(s\) to \(\beta_*+20e\), still keeping \(w=3\). On
retained heights move its segment to \(a+16e\). The denominator's
zero-free buffer permits this last move for every presentation in the
bin; outside those heights leave the reciprocal on the global line.
The entire deformation lies in (B0.34). There is no nonprincipal numerator
pole, and no \(z\)-pole for \(\Re z\ge z_0\).

Use the exact expansion (B0.33), fix a main-prime amplitude class, and now
perform the full \(w\)-inversion on its original absolute line. The
reciprocal is independent of \(w\). (B0.40) and (B0.41), and the
buffered subpower reciprocal bound, give

\[
\sum_{u\ \text{ in the class}}^{(6)}
\left|\frac{q_u^{-z}\mathcal N_u(Y;s,z)}
{L_{\mathbb K}^S(s,\eta\overline{\psi_u})}\right|
\ll (1+T)^A Y^{-1/2}
Z^{\ell(z_0-1/2)+\ell q+\varepsilon_2}
U^{1/4+3R_\kappa/4-z_0-qz_A(d)/2+\varepsilon_2},
\tag{B0.53}
\]

where

\[
z_A(d)=\frac{2\min(y/d,1)-1}{6\kappa},\qquad
d z_A(d)=\frac{\min(d,2y-d)}{6\kappa}.
\tag{B0.54}
\]

For sufficiently small \(\zeta_0\), this capacity is positive and
available. The independent heights of the physical prime sums and the
detector witnesses are covered by the moment seminorm bounds; no
common physical/witness height is asserted.

Multiplying (B0.53) by the remaining factors in (B0.28), and subtracting
\(\beta_*-k\), gives exactly

\[
a-\beta_*+h(z_0-1/6)-y/2-\ell/2+\ell q
+d(1/4+3R_\kappa/4-z_0)
-\frac q{12\kappa}\min(d,2y-d).
\tag{B0.55}
\]

At \(d=h\) this is \(F^{(4)}_\kappa(\delta,p)-\beta_*\), with
\(F^{(4)}\) as in (B0.47). Its convexity in \(d\), the endpoint bounds
in §B0.6, and the floor estimate therefore supply a fixed negative
margin on the whole retained interval. The extension above \(h\) costs
at most a fixed multiple of \(\zeta_0\). Dyadic sums, amplitude classes,
and finite profile-height costs fit inside a reserved fraction of this
margin.

All witness capacities are available because
\(\ell/(h+\zeta_0)>4/21\). The new numerator capacity is available
because \(\min(d,2y-d)\le y<4\ell\le6\kappa\ell\).
If \(\ell_{\max}\) is the largest base-\(Z\) slot length, its largest
relative length on the retained range is at most
\(\ell_{\max}/d_{\min}\). Finitely many sufficiently short equal
slots, on disjoint norm subintervals, therefore meet both the MP mesh and
the greedy rounding condition uniformly, including the smallest dyads.
title: Retained nonprincipal rows

statement:
# Source authorship and dependency notices

The mathematical source payload is reused from the pinned OpenAI project and the exact selected additive extension project. Upstream file headers, names, copyrights and proof bodies are preserved. The original OpenAI project's license is copied byte-for-byte as `lean/UPSTREAM-LICENSE` and also remains at `project/LICENSE` in the source archive. This document does not replace or broaden that license.

`DEPENDENCY-LICENSES.json` identifies every locked dependency by upstream URL and exact revision, and lists the license/notice entries actually included in the source archive. Existing dependency notices and copyright headers are preserved, including differently licensed notices such as Unicode data notices. Dependency code is not represented as newly authored by this release's maintainers.

Ten earlier local snapshots lacked a standalone license file: `belyi`, `formal-schemes`, `tempered-fundamental-groups`, `oka`, `orbicurve-cores`, `heights`, `genl`, `tate-curves-theta`, `gromov`, and `StrongPNT`. Inspection of the actual 12,205-module terminal closure showed zero modules from all ten. Their full source trees, metadata copies and license-less compatibility source snapshots are excluded from this public payload. Their precise upstream pins remain as fetched-only configuration dependencies; no license is assigned to those repositories. Every dependency whose actual proof sources are vendored has a preserved standalone license.

The 23 compatibility patch files are still needed by the unchanged Lake configuration. They are exact Git blobs under `lean/patches` in the pinned OpenAI commit. The verbatim upstream repository root license is included as `OPENAI-REPOSITORY-LICENSE`; `OPENAI-LICENSE-PATCH-PROVENANCE.json` records the byte-for-byte comparisons. The recipient recipe applies these exact retained patches inside freshly fetched, isolated dependency checkouts before restoring the loaded-source overlay. This avoids redistributing gratuitous unused package source copies while retaining the original build configuration and exact proof bytes. Repository-level license and new-extension attribution choices remain with the publication owner.

The compatibility patches in the source archive are exact reviewed build-compatibility files from the admitted project. They include substantive changes. Source provenance and revision data are retained separately from the mathematical admission: a pinned dependency, copied license or checksum is not itself a theorem proof.
title: Source authorship and dependency notices

  2 * D.t + 26 * D.e + (D.N + 8) * D.eps + D.t +
      totalE * D.t + D.t / 8 + D.sigma + 32 * rho0 / 25 ≤ 7 / 1200

`slot_aware_floor_budget` would miss the fixed `32*rho0/25` term.
-/

theorem finite_central_band_sum {N : ℕ}
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hmax : ∀ P ∈ S, P.IsMaximal)
    (η : Character) (rows : Finset FreeRow) (T : Fin N → Finset ProbePhysical.PrimeIdeal)
    (hT : ∀ j P, P ∈ T j → P.val ∉ S) (W : Fin N → ℝ → ℂ) (Yp : Fin N → ℝ)
    (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (X Y Z e heightBase upper C exponent : ℝ)
    (idx grid : FreeRow → ℕ) (n m : ℕ)
    (hrows : ∀ u ∈ rows, u.val ≠ 1 ∧ rowNorm u ≤ upper)
    (hlabel : ∀ u ∈ rows, idx u ≤ n ∧ grid u ≤ m) (_hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hcell : ∀ k ∈ smallDyadicIndices upper, ∀ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
      ∀ j ∈ Finset.range (m + 1),
      ‖finiteCentralCubeRows S hS hmax η (cubeBinRows (rows ∩ dyadicRows 1 k) idx grid i j)
        T hT W Yp W0 W1 X Y Z e (fun _ => 51 / 100 + e * j)
        (fun _ => (3 * i + 1 : ℕ) * heightBase)‖ ≤ C * Z ^ exponent) :
    ‖finiteCentralCubeRows S hS hmax η rows T hT W Yp W0 W1 X Y Z e
      (fun u => 51 / 100 + e * grid u) (fun u => (3 * idx u + 1 : ℕ) * heightBase)‖ ≤
      (smallDyadicIndices upper).card * (n + 1 : ℕ) * (m + 1 : ℕ) * C * Z ^ exponent
title: finite_central_band_sum

  character := η
  puncture := 1
  radial := {
    keep := sourcePlainKeep η
    profile := Φ
    scale := U
    scale_pos := zero_lt_one.trans_le hU
    nonneg := fun z => hp _ }
  rowWidth := 1
  characterWidth := δ

  row_nonneg := by norm_num
  character_nonneg := hδ
  scale_eq := by simp
  modulus_bound := by simpa only [one_mul] using hη
  puncture_ne_zero := one_ne_zero
  puncture_bound := by simp [Ideal.radical_top]
  radial_support := hs

statement:
def unramifiedErrorCoefficients (Q : ℝ) (A eta v x z : ℂ) : CubicCoefficients :=
  let V := coordV Q z
  let D := coordD Q eta v x
  let B := star eta * (Q : ℂ) ^ x
  let nu := star v
  let E₀ := unramifiedE₀ Q A eta v x z
  let E₁ := unramifiedE₁ Q A eta v x z
  let c := (1 - V) / (1 - D)
  let a := errorBracketConstant V D B nu E₀
  let b := errorBracketLinear V D B nu E₀ E₁
  let d := errorBracketQuadratic E₁
  ⟨c * a, c * (b - v * a), c * (d - v * b), -c * v * d⟩
title: unramifiedErrorCoefficients

    (Lmod Lslot loss lo hi κ : ℝ) (hLm : 0≤Lmod) (hLs : 0≤Lslot) (hloss : 0<loss)
     (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) :
    ∃degree : ℕ,∃S : Finset (ℕ×ℕ),∃C : ℝ,0<C ∧
    ∀η₀ : Character,∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,
    ∀(θ : α→RayQuotient.Characters M H)(w σ v : α→ℝ)(t T : ℝ),
      (∀i∈F,0≤w i) → (∀i∈F,w i≤Lslot) →
      (∀i∈F,lo≤σ i) → (∀i∈F,σ i≤hi) → 0≤T → (∀i∈F,|v i|≤T) →
    ∀(η : Character)(Q : Ideal O)(r : Radial)(Qbound : ℝ),Q≤M → 0≤Qbound →
      (∀z,r.keep z→z≠0) →
      (∀z,r.keep z→¬FixedInducingRow η (internalQ Q η₀) fixedBadMask 1 z) →
      (∀z,r.keep z→((naturalCharacter η z).modulus.absNorm:ℝ)≤Z^Lmod) →
      (∀z,r.keep z→((naturalCharacter η z).modulus.absNorm:ℝ)≤Qbound) →
    ∀(W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ,ℂ)),Function.support (W₁:ℝ→ℂ)⊆Set.Icc a₀ b₀ →
      Function.support (W₂:ℝ→ℂ)⊆Set.Icc a₀ b₀ →
    ∀X₁ X₂ : ℝ,0<X₁ → 0<X₂ → ∀A : Finset α,A⊆F →
      radialEnergy (fun z=>polynomial (naturalCharacter η z) false W₁ X₁ 0 0*
        polynomial (naturalCharacter η z) false W₂ X₂ 0 0*
        ∏i∈A,naturalSlot (naturalCharacter η z) (primePool M H b (Z^(w i)))

            HeckePrimeAnnular.annularWeight W (Z^(w i)) (σ i) (v i) I) t) (Z^(w i)))
        r.keep r.profile r.scale ≤

        ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁)*
         (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂))^2*Qbound^4*

    length Z X₁+length Z X₂+6*κ*(∑i,w i)≤s.width→

statement:
theorem masked_natural_pair_slots {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (F : Finset α) (W : ℝ→ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0<a)
    (hWs : Function.support W⊆Set.Icc a b) (hW : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W)
    (a₀ b₀ ε : ℝ) (ha₀ : 0<a₀) (hb₀ : 0≤b₀) (hε : 0<ε)
    (Lmod Lslot loss lo hi κ : ℝ) (hLm : 0≤Lmod) (hLs : 0≤Lslot) (hloss : 0<loss)
     (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) :
    ∃degree : ℕ,∃S : Finset (ℕ×ℕ),∃C : ℝ,0<C ∧
    ∀η₀ : Character,∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,
    ∀(θ : α→RayQuotient.Characters M H)(w σ v : α→ℝ)(t T : ℝ),
      (∀i∈F,0≤w i) → (∀i∈F,w i≤Lslot) →
      (∀i∈F,lo≤σ i) → (∀i∈F,σ i≤hi) → 0≤T → (∀i∈F,|v i|≤T) →
    ∀(η : Character)(Q : Ideal O)(r : Radial)(Qbound : ℝ)(R : Ideal O),R≠0 → Q≤M → 0≤Qbound →
      (∀z,r.keep z→z≠0) →
      (∀z,r.keep z→¬FixedInducingRow η (internalQ Q η₀) fixedBadMask 1 z) →
      (∀z,r.keep z→((naturalCharacter η z).modulus.absNorm:ℝ)≤Z^Lmod) →
      (∀z,r.keep z→((naturalCharacter η z).modulus.absNorm:ℝ)≤Qbound) →
    ∀(W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ,ℂ)),Function.support (W₁:ℝ→ℂ)⊆Set.Icc a₀ b₀ →
      Function.support (W₂:ℝ→ℂ)⊆Set.Icc a₀ b₀ →
    ∀X₁ X₂ : ℝ,0<X₁ → 0<X₂ →
      radialEnergy (fun z=>polynomial (excluded (naturalCharacter η z) R) false W₁ X₁ 0 0*
        polynomial (excluded (naturalCharacter η z) R) false W₂ X₂ 0 0*
        ∏i∈F,naturalSlot (excluded (naturalCharacter η z) R) (primePool M H b (Z^(w i)))
          (heightCoefficient (fun I=>idealCoeff (relativeCharacter M H hH η₀ (θ i)) I*
            HeckePrimeAnnular.annularWeight W (Z^(w i)) (σ i) (v i) I) t) (Z^(w i)))
        r.keep r.profile r.scale ≤
      C*(R.radical.absNorm:ℝ)^ε*diagonalControl r.profile*max 1 r.scale*
        ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁)*
         (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂))^2*Qbound^4*
         (1+|t|+T)^degree*Z^(loss+κ*(∑i∈F,w i))
title: masked_natural_pair_slots

theorem weighted_principal_product_error {κ ι : Type*} (S : Finset κ)
    (T : κ → Finset ι) (w Q : κ → ι → ℝ) (A η : κ → ι → ℂ)
    (s : ℂ) (P : ℝ) (hP : 480 ≤ P) (hs : theta ≤ s.re)
    (hw : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, 0 ≤ w j i)
    (hQ : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, P ≤ Q j i)
    (hA : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, ‖A j i‖ ≤ 1)
    (hη : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, ‖η j i‖ = 1)
    (hM : ∀ j ∈ S, 0 < ∑ i ∈ T j, w j i) :
    ‖(∏ j ∈ S, ∑ i ∈ T j, (w j i : ℂ) * principalSlot (Q j i) (A j i) (η j i) s) /
        principalScalar S (fun j => ∑ i ∈ T j, w j i) - 1‖ ≤
      (1 + 1440 * P ^ (-theta)) ^ S.card - 1
title: weighted_principal_product_error

statement:
theorem row_original_split (S : Finset (Ideal O))
    (hS : ∀ P ∈ S, Prime P) (u : FreeRow)
    (hn : (rowCharacter S hS u).residue ≠ 1) :
    ∃ (τ ψ : Character) (g : ℂ),
      (∀ n : O, elementCoeff (rowCharacter S hS u) n = elementCoeff τ n) ∧
      (∀ I : Ideal O, idealCoeff (rowCharacter S hS u).inverse I = idealCoeff τ.inverse I) ∧
      τ.residue ≠ 1 ∧ FiniteFourier.IsPrimitiveOnIdeals ψ.residue ∧
      ψ.residue ≠ 1 ∧ ‖g‖ = 1 ∧
      τ.modulus.absNorm ≤ fixedConductorConstant S *
        (Ideal.span {u.val} : Ideal O).radical.absNorm ∧
      ψ.modulus.absNorm * (redundantIdeal τ.modulus ψ.modulus).absNorm ≤
        τ.modulus.absNorm ∧
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (P : Fin k → Ideal O), (∀ i, Prime (P i)) →
        Function.Injective P → ∀ (e : Fin k → ℕ), (∀ i, 2 ≤ e i) →
        (∀ i, P i ^ e i ∣ Ideal.span {u.val}) →
        (ψ.modulus.absNorm * (redundantIdeal τ.modulus ψ.modulus).absNorm) *
          ∏ i, (P i).absNorm ^ (e i - 1) ≤
            fixedConductorConstant S * (Ideal.span {u.val} : Ideal O).absNorm) ∧
      ∀ (G : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (X R : ℝ), 0 < X →
        HeckeDyadic.polynomial (rowCharacter S hS u) false G X 0 0 =
          g * (retainedSchwartz τ ψ G X R + discardedSchwartz τ ψ G X R)

statement:
private def applyDependencyPatch (plan : PatchPlan) (directory : FilePath) : IO Unit := do
  let applied ← patchGit directory #["apply", plan.patch.toString]
  unless applied.exitCode == 0 do
    throw <| IO.userError s!"{plan.label}: failed to apply compatibility patch:\n{applied.stderr}"
  let verified ← checkPatch directory plan.patch #["--reverse"]
  unless verified.exitCode == 0 do
    throw <| IO.userError s!"{plan.label}: patch verification failed:\n{verified.stderr}"

/-- Prepare patched package configurations before Lake resolves their dependencies. -/
title: applyDependencyPatch

## 2. The probe and its reciprocal signal

We use just the scales needed for \(4/33\):
\[
\begin{gathered}
 X=Z^x,\quad Y=Z^y,\quad P=Z^\ell,\qquad
 (x,y,\ell)=\left(\frac{13}{33},\frac{15}{33},\frac5{33}\right),\\
 h=1+\ell-x=\frac{25}{33},\qquad k=\frac56-\frac x3-\frac\ell6=\frac{67}{99}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{2.1}
\]
The temporary independent variables \(X,Y,Z\) below make the two exact representations transparent.

statement:
structure WeightedCellRowData {Δ : ℝ} (D : WeightedQRH.HighParameters.HighData Δ)
    (F : WeightedSourceData D.toMomentData) (η : Character) (Z τ : ℝ)
    (idx grid : FreeRow→ℕ) (n k i j : ℕ) : Prop where
  a_lower : (51/100:ℝ) < 51/100+D.e*j
  a_upper : (51/100:ℝ)+D.e*j ≤ 7/8
  d_lower : (1/200:ℝ) ≤ sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k
  d_upper : sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k ≤ 7/8
  index_le : i ≤ n
  rows_source : ∀u∈weightedCellRows D F Z idx grid k i j,
    u.val≠1 ∧ Z^(1/100:ℝ) ≤ rowNorm u ∧
      (calibrationForSet F.S F.maximal).residueMonoid u.val≠0 ∧
      rowNorm u ≤ Z^(sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k-D.t)
  rows_moment : ∀u∈weightedCellRows D F Z idx grid k i j,
    (Z^(sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k))^(1/100:ℝ) ≤ rowNorm u ∧
      rowNorm u ≤ Z^(sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k)
  rows_nonprincipal : ∀u∈weightedCellRows D F Z idx grid k i j,
    (rowCharacter F.S F.exclusions.prime u).residue≠1
  rows_frequency : ∀u∈weightedCellRows D F Z idx grid k i j,
    Z^(sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k-2*D.t) ≤ rowNorm u
  next : ∀u∈weightedCellRows D F Z idx grid k i j,
    detectorMaximum
      (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
      (3*(i+1:ℕ)*Z^τ) < 51/100+D.e*j+2*D.e
  current : ∀u∈weightedCellRows D F Z idx grid k i j,
    (51/100:ℝ)+D.e*j ≤ detectorMaximum
      (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
      ((3*i:ℕ)*Z^τ)
title: WeightedCellRowData

statement:
### 2.4. The principal signal

Only \(u=1\) has a principal numerator. The inertia calculation excludes nonunits. For a unit \(u\), choose by CRT a primary \(n\), prime to \(S\), congruent to \(-2-3\omega\) modulo \(36\) and to one at the other excluded primes. Then \(q_n\equiv7\pmod{36}\), and multiplicativity gives \(\chi_n(u)=u^{(q_n-1)/6}=u\). This excludes the five other units.

Write \(\rho_S=\operatorname{Res}_{s=1}\zeta_K^S(s)>0\) and
\[
 c_S=\frac{\rho_S^2}{6}\widehat W_1(1)\mathscr M(1/6)>0.
\tag{2.18}
\]
For \(0<\sigma<1\), Fourier duality against a Gaussian, followed by its positive integral representation, gives
\[
 \mathscr M(\sigma)=\left(\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt3}\right)^{1-2\sigma}
 \frac{\Gamma(\sigma)}{\Gamma(1-\sigma)}
 \int_0^\infty W_0(r)r^{-\sigma}\,dr>0.
\]
Absolute convergence follows from the annular support and the Schwartz transform. The factor \(1/6\) in \(c_S\) comes from the pole of \(\zeta_K^S(6z)\).

At \(w=1,z=1/6\), set \(t=Q^{-1}\), \(D=\eta(\mathfrak p)Q^{-s}\), and \(R=\overline{\alpha(\mathfrak p)}^6\eta(\mathfrak p)^6Q^{3-6s}\). The local table simplifies to
\[
 H_{\eta,\mathfrak p}(s)=\frac{1-t^2}{1-R}
 \left(1+\frac{t(D-R)}{1-D}\right),\qquad
 H_{\eta,\mathfrak p}(s)-1\ll Q^{-2}+Q^{-1-\Re s}+Q^{3-6\Re s}.
\tag{2.19}
\]
Increasing the fixed cutoff makes the sum of this majorant sufficiently small that
\[
 H_\eta(s):=H_{\eta,1}(s,1,1/6),\qquad
 |H_\eta(s)-1|\le\tfrac12\quad(\Re s\ge87/100).
\tag{2.20}
\]
At this residue (2.12) gives \(G_{\mathfrak p}/H_{\mathfrak p}=-1+O(Q^{-87/100})\). Put
\[
 A(Z)=-P^{-1/6}\sum_{\mathfrak p\notin S}w(Q/P)Q^{-5/6}.
\tag{2.21}
\]
The fixed-field prime ideal theorem gives \(|A(Z)|\asymp(\log Z)^{-1}\) for sufficiently large \(Z\), and, for every fixed \(0<\mu_P<(87/100)\ell\),
\[
 \mathcal H_{\eta,1,Z}(s,1,1/6)
 =H_\eta(s)Z^{\ell/6}A(Z)(1+O(Z^{-\mu_P})),\qquad \Re s\ge87/100.
\tag{2.22}
\]
Define, for large \(Z\), \(J_\eta(Z)=I_\eta^{\rm comp}(Z)/(c_SA(Z))\), and for every \(Z>0\),
\[
 f_\eta(Z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(2)}Z^{s-k}e^{(s-5/6)^2}
 \frac{H_\eta(s)}{L_K^S(s,\eta)}\,ds.
\tag{2.23}
\]
The double residue of (2.8) is \(f_\eta\), up to the power-small error in (2.22). The factor \(Z^{\ell/6}\), not the logarithmic prime density, is the gain from compensation.

statement:
structure PhysicalReflectionData (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : ∀P∈S,Prime P) (u : FreeRow) where
  presentation : Character
  primitive : Character
  phase : ℂ
  element_eq : ∀n:O,elementCoeff (rowCharacter S hS u) n=elementCoeff presentation n
  inverse_eq : ∀J:Ideal O,idealCoeff (rowCharacter S hS u).inverse J=idealCoeff presentation.inverse J
  phase_norm : ‖phase‖=1
  conductor_bound : primitive.modulus.absNorm*(redundantIdeal presentation.modulus primitive.modulus).absNorm≤
    fixedConductorConstant S*(Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).radical.absNorm
  split : ∀(G:𝓢(ℝ,ℂ))(X R:ℝ),0<X→
    HeckeDyadic.polynomial (rowCharacter S hS u) false G X 0 0=
      phase*(retainedSchwartz presentation primitive G X R+discardedSchwartz presentation primitive G X R)

statement:
theorem fiber_count_from_raw {Row Label : Type*}
    (rows : Finset Row) (χ : Row → Label → Character)
    (U a ε T allowance height εm Ci Cs : ℝ) (i : ℕ)
    (hU : 1 < U) (ha : 1 / 2 ≤ a) (hδu : 2 * a - 1 ≤ 5 / 6)
    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hCi : 0 ≤ Ci) (hCs : 0 ≤ Cs) (hh : 0 ≤ height)
    (hf : 2 * Real.pi * allowance + (3 * i : ℕ) * T ≤ height)
    (w : ∀ u, SupportedWitness (χ u) U a ε (t0 (2 * a - 1)) T allowance i)
    (label : Label) (J K : Fin (dyadicLength U))
    (hl : ∀ u ∈ rows, (w u).label = label)
    (hJ : ∀ u ∈ rows, (w u).left = J) (hK : ∀ u ∈ rows, (w u).right = K)
    (hMraw : ∀ n : ℕ, n ≤ 2 → ∀ σ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      ∀ freq ∈ Icc (-height) height,
      ∑ u ∈ rows, ‖polynomial (χ u label) true
        ((logProfile^[n]) (inverseTest U (t0 (2 * a - 1))
          (Real.logb U ((2 : ℝ) ^ J.val))))
        (U ^ (Real.logb U ((2 : ℝ) ^ J.val))) σ freq‖ ^ 2 ≤
        Ci * U ^ (inverseExponent (Real.logb U ((2 : ℝ) ^ J.val)) + εm))
    (hSraw : PlainRawAt rows χ label U (Real.logb U ((2 : ℝ) ^ K.val)) height εm Cs) :
    (rows.card : ℝ) ≤ max (12 * (1 + height) * Ci) (192 * (1 + height) * Cs) *
      U ^ (Exponent.R0 (2 * a - 1) + 6 * ε + εm)

def actualRamifiedErrorCoefficients (η : Character) (u : FreeRow) (P : PrimeIdeal)
    (hs : Supported P.val) (x z : ℂ) : CubicCoefficients :=
  let p := primaryGenerator P.val
  let hp := supported_primeGenerator_prime P hs
  letI : (Ideal.span {p} : Ideal O).IsMaximal := PrincipalIdealRing.isMaximal_of_irreducible hp.irreducible
  let hsp : Supported (Ideal.span {p}) := (span_primaryGenerator_of_supported P.val hs).symm ▸ hs
  let hg := (supported_prime_data p hp hsp).1
  ramifiedErrorCoefficients p hp hg (targetMonoid η p) (actualACube η p)
    (actualSextic (Ideal.span {p}) hg (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (unitPart u p hp)))
    x z (multiplicity p u.val)
title: actualRamifiedErrorCoefficients

statement:
\begin{proposition}[Checked original-numerator moment]\label{prop:checked-original-fourth}
Assume $51/100\le\beta_*$. \textup{(}The bound $\beta_*\le7/8$ of
\cite{openai} is available throughout but is not needed here; the Lean
statement assumes only the lower bound.\textup{)}
Fix the original weighted source data, its moment loss $t>0$, a
Schwartz profile $G$, and positive constants $\lambda,\xi,b$.
For sufficiently large $U$, let $\mathcal R$ be any finite set of
nonprincipal physical rows with $U^{1/100}\le q_u\le U$.
For every row choose $0<N_u\le bY$, where $Y>0$, and its actual
combined conductor $C_u$. Suppose, for a common $m\ge0$,
\[
 m+\xi\le2,\qquad
 C_u\le C_S U^m\frac{Y}{N_u}.
\]
Let $T$ be any selected family of original prime slots with nonnegative
widths $r_i$ below the certified mesh
$\operatorname{fineMesh}(2,0,1,3/4,t/4)$, and let
$\Re z_i=17/50$, $|\Im z_i|\le H$, $H\ge0$. Assume
\[
 2(m+\xi)+\frac92\sum_{i\in T}r_i\le1
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad T=\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \left|\prod_{i\in T}Q_i(u;z_i)\right|\le U.
\]
Then there are a fixed integer $J\ge0$ and $C>0$ such that
\[
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal R}
 \left|S_{\chi_u}(Y/N_u;G)\right|^4
 \left|\prod_{i\in T}Q_i(u;z_i)\right|^2
 \le C(1+H)^J U^{1+t+\lambda}.
\]
The constants and threshold precede all choices of rows, scales,
selected slots, and heights. They may depend on the fixed source data,
profile and displayed fixed positive constants.
\end{proposition}
title: prop:checked-original-fourth

statement:
#### Mellin continuation

Choose the \(\varepsilon\) in (B0.50) smaller than \(\mu/4\), and reduce \(\Delta\), if necessary, so that \(\Delta<\mu/4\). Equations (B0.50)–(B0.51) imply

\[
f_\eta(Z)\ll_\eta Z^{\beta_*-k-\Delta}\qquad(Z\longrightarrow\infty).
\tag{B0.59}
\]

For \(0<Z\le1\), move the defining line in (B0.36) to any fixed \(A>2\). Absolute Euler convergence, the Gaussian, and (B0.35) give
\[
f_\eta(Z)=O_{\eta,A}(Z^{A-k}).
\tag{B0.60}
\]
Consequently

\[
\mathfrak F_\eta(s)=\int_0^\infty f_\eta(Z)Z^{-s+k}\,\frac{dZ}{Z}
\tag{B0.61}
\]

is holomorphic on \(\Re s>\beta_*-\Delta\). On \(\Re s>1\), Fourier inversion in \(\log Z\), first on a fixed vertical line, identifies it with

\[
\mathfrak F_\eta(s)=
e^{(s-5/6)^2}\frac{H_\eta(s)}{L_{\mathbb K}^S(s,\eta)}.
\tag{B0.62}
\]

The Fourier density on that line is integrable by Gaussian decay. Its inverse transform is integrable by (B0.59)–(B0.60), which justifies the identification as an ordinary Mellin integral. Identity on the full half-plane \(\Re s>1\) also follows by analytic continuation from any intervening strip of absolute integrability.

Choose \(\Delta\) additionally so that \(\beta_*-\Delta>b_0>87/100\). Formula (B0.35) and the nonvanishing Gaussian show that the right side of (B0.62) would have a pole at every zero of \(L_{\mathbb K}^S(s,\eta)\) in this half-plane. Its holomorphic continuation (B0.61) excludes all such zeros. This conclusion holds for each primitive finite-order target, with the same real boundary \(\beta_*-\Delta\). Constants and thresholds may depend on the target; the excluded strip does not. It contradicts the definition of \(\beta_*\). Thus \(\beta_*\le b_0\).

The classical nonvanishing on \(\Re s=1\) and the Euler product on \(\Re s>1\) complete the asserted half-plane statement. Finally

\[
\zeta_{\mathbb K}(s)=\zeta(s)L(s,\chi_{-3}).
\tag{B0.63}
\]

The second factor is holomorphic in the relevant strip. A zeta zero there would be a zero of the principal Hecke function, which has just been excluded. Reflection by the zeta functional equation gives the stated symmetric location of nontrivial zeros. This proves Theorem B0.
title: Mellin continuation

    (T : Finset HeckeInverseAmplification.PrimeIdeal) (hT : ∀ P ∈ T, Supported P.val)

    (x z : ℂ) (alpha eps rho L : ℝ) (hQ : ∀ P ∈ T, (4 : ℝ) ≤ P.val.absNorm)
    (halpha : (51 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ alpha) (halpha1 : alpha ≤ 1)
    (heps : 0 < eps) (heps1 : eps ≤ 1 / 1000)
    (hx : x.re = alpha + 16 * eps) (hz : z.re = 17 / 50)
    (hrho : 0 ≤ rho) (hrho1 : rho ≤ 1)
    (hline : 1 - alpha - 6 * eps ≤ 1 / 2 - rho)
    (hleft : -(1 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2 - rho)
    (hmargin : 1 + firsteps ≤ x.re + (1 / 2 - rho))
    (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hcap : L * errorProductDeficit u T ≤ 1) :
    Summable (fun e : ErrorPacketIndex S u T => ‖errorPacketCoefficient S hS η u T hT x z e‖ *
      (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ)^(-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) *
      max 1 (L * (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ))^rho) ∧
    (∑' e : ErrorPacketIndex S u T, ‖errorPacketCoefficient S hS η u T hT x z e‖ *
      (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ)^(-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) *
      max 1 (L * (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ))^rho) ≤
      2 * (579 ^ (ramifiedPrimes (markExclusions S T) u).card * Real.exp (1 / 2) *
        errorProductSize u T)

statement:
# The quartic QRH boundary

Hailey Collet  
HaileyCollet@gmail.com

We prove a strict zero-free half-plane for every finite-order Hecke character of trivial infinite type over \(\mathbf Q(\omega)\), and hence for all complex Dirichlet characters and the Riemann zeta function. The boundary is defined by an isolated quartic root. The proof combines finite sextic identities, completed reflection, common-profile moments and a compensated physical probe. The positive-slot moment is used only in its proved common-profile range \(7/10\le\kappa\le3/4\). Stable labels B0–B4 identify the analytic arguments; T0–T4 state the boundary and its character transfers.
title: The quartic QRH boundary

theorem calibratedTupleValue_error_subsets {K : ℕ}
    (eps : ℝ) (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (htail : FirstTail eps S)
    (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal) (P : Fin K→PrimeIdeal) (hP : Function.Injective P)
    (hPS : ∀i,(P i).val∉S) (η : Character) (u : FreeRow)
    (W : Fin K→ℝ→ℂ) (Y : Fin K→ℝ) (x w z : ℂ)
    (hx : (51/100:ℝ)≤x.re) (hz : (17/50:ℝ)≤z.re)
    (hw : -(1/100:ℝ)≤w.re) (hxw : 1+eps≤x.re+w.re) :
    calibratedTupleValue S hS hmax η u P hPS W Y x w z=
      numeratorFreeRowScalar S hS hmax η u x z*
      HeckeOrigin.continued (rowCharacter S hS.prime u) w*
      (∑I∈Finset.univ.powerset,weightedErrorTuple S hS η u I P hPS W Y x w z*
        physicalMainTuple u I P W Y z)
title: calibratedTupleValue_error_subsets

statement:
def audit (modules roots : Array Name) : CommandElabM Unit := do
  let env := (← getEnv).setExporting false
  for module in modules do
    unless env.header.moduleNames.contains module do
      throwError "missing audited module {module}"
  let mut declarations : Array Name := #[]
  let mut theorems : Array Name := #[]
  let mut customAxioms : Array Name := #[]
  for (n, ci) in env.constants.toList do
    let owned := match env.getModuleIdxFor? n with
      | some m => modules.contains env.header.moduleNames[m.toNat]!
      | none => false
    if owned then
      declarations := declarations.push n
      match ci with
      | .thmInfo _ => theorems := theorems.push n
      | .axiomInfo _ => customAxioms := customAxioms.push n
      | _ => pure ()
  unless customAxioms.isEmpty do
    throwError "analytic source declares axioms: {customAxioms}"
  unless !theorems.isEmpty do
    throwError "no analytic theorems were discovered"
  for root in roots do
    unless theorems.contains root do
      throwError "required theorem is missing from audited modules: {root}"
  let mut axiomReports : Array Json := #[]
  for root in declarations do
    let axioms ← collectAxioms root
    let forbidden := axioms.filter fun n => !allowedAxiom n
    unless forbidden.isEmpty do
      throwError "forbidden axioms in {root}: {forbidden}"
    axiomReports := axiomReports.push (Json.mkObj [
      ("declaration", toJson root.toString),
      ("axioms", toJson (axioms.map Name.toString))])
  let mut todo := declarations
  let mut seen : NameSet := {}
  let mut idx := 0
  let mut forbidden : Array Name := #[]
  let mut missing : Array Name := #[]
  while idx < todo.size do
    let n := todo[idx]!
    idx := idx + 1
    if seen.contains n then continue
    seen := seen.insert n
    if forbiddenTerminal env n then forbidden := forbidden.push n
    match env.find? n with
    | none => missing := missing.push n
    | some ci =>
      for dep in ci.getUsedConstantsAsSet.toArray do
        todo := todo.push dep
  let report := Json.mkObj [
    ("modules", toJson (modules.map Name.toString)),
    ("required_roots", toJson (roots.map Name.toString)),
    ("declaration_count", toJson declarations.size),
    ("theorem_count", toJson theorems.size),
    ("theorems", toJson (theorems.map Name.toString)),
    ("axiom_reports", toJson axiomReports),
    ("all_reachable_constants", toJson seen.size),
    ("forbidden_terminal_dependencies", toJson (forbidden.map Name.toString)),
    ("missing_declarations", toJson (missing.map Name.toString))]
  logInfo m!"ANALYTIC_AUDIT {report.compress}"
  unless forbidden.isEmpty && missing.isEmpty do
    throwError "analytic dependency audit failed"

/-- The standalone mixed moment may not depend on either terminal zero-free
result, the former beta-lower-bound wrappers, or disposable extraction modules. -/
title: audit

statement:
def errorLabelNumerator {K : ℕ} (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S)
    (η : Character) (u : FreeRow) (J : Finset (Fin K))
    (T : Fin K→Finset HeckeInverseAmplification.PrimeIdeal)
    (hT : ∀i P,P∈T i→P.val∉S) (W : Fin K→ℝ→ℂ) (Yp : Fin K→ℝ)
    (x z : ℂ) (W1 : ℝ→ℂ) (Y : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  ∑P:(∀i:J,T i.val),(∏i:J,physicalSlotWeight (P i).val (W i.val) (Yp i.val) z)*
    errorNumeratorIntegral S hS η u (Finset.univ.image (fun i:J=>(P i).val))
      (partial_image_supported S hS J T hT P) x z W1 Y

/-- The normalized full-w integral of the actual calibrated prime tuples equals
its error-label numerators times the remaining, unaltered prime sums. -/
title: errorLabelNumerator

statement:
def SameDataCanonicalPhysicalAt
    {Delta : ℝ} (D : HighDataPerturbed Delta)
    (hfine : ∀j, D.ell j ≤ detectorMesh D.t / 200)
    (F : PerturbedSourceData (momentGeometryOfPerturbed D hfine))
    (theta : ℝ) : Prop :=
  letI : NeZero (∏P∈F.S, P) :=
    ⟨fixedPrimeProduct_ne_zero F.S F.exclusions.prime⟩
  ∃n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∀eta : Character, ∃C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,
      let Y : Fin D.N → ℝ := fun j => Z ^ (D.ell j)
      let T : Fin D.N → Finset PrimeIdeal := fun j =>
        pool (RayQuotient.identityClass F.modulus ⊤) F.S 1 2 (Y j)
      let hT := canonicalPoolOutside (M := F.modulus) (⊤) F.S D.N 1 2 Y
      let normer := sourceResidueConstant F.W F.W (∏P∈F.S, P) *
        (Probe.principalScalar Finset.univ Z totalE
          (slotMass T (residueWeights (fun _ => F.w) Y)) : ℂ)
      normer ≠ 0 ∧ ∃idx grid : FreeRow → ℕ,
      (∀u, 1 ≤ idx u ∧ idx u ≤ n ∧
        grid u ≤ ⌊(49 / 100 : ℝ) / D.e⌋₊ ∧
        ((3 * idx u + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Z ^ theta + Z ^ theta / 2 ≤
          (3 * idx u + 2 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) ∧
      (∀u, let alpha : ℝ := 51 / 100 + D.e * grid u
        (51 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ alpha ∧ alpha ≤ 1 ∧
        alpha ≤ detectorMaximum
          (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
            (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
          (3 * idx u * Z ^ theta) ∧
        detectorMaximum
          (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
            (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
          (3 * idx u * Z ^ theta) < alpha + D.e ∧
        detectorMaximum
          (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
            (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
          (3 * (idx u + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) < alpha + 2 * D.e ∧
        ((51 / 100 : ℝ) < alpha → ∃j s,
          LFunction
            (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
              (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u) j) s = 0 ∧
          ¬((sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
              (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u) j).residue = 1 ∧ s = 1) ∧
          alpha ≤ s.re ∧ s.re < alpha + D.e ∧
          |s.im| ≤ 3 * idx u * Z ^ theta)) ∧
      (∀u∈rowBand (Z ^ (1 / 100 : ℝ)) (Z ^ (physicalHeight + D.t)),
        (calibrationForSet F.S F.maximal).residueMonoid u.val ≠ 0 →
        (∀chi, (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u chi).residue ≠ 1) ∧
        (∀chi, (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u chi).modulus.absNorm ≤
          conductorConstant * F.modulus.absNorm *
            (Ideal.span {u.val} : Ideal O).absNorm) ∧
        ∀hnp : ∀chi, (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u chi).residue ≠ 1,
          HeckeDetectorZeros.zeroMaximum (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u) hnp
            (3 * (idx u + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) <
              51 / 100 + D.e * grid u + 2 * D.e) ∧
      let rows := rowBand (Z ^ (1 / 100 : ℝ)) (Z ^ (physicalHeight + D.t))
      let alpha : FreeRow → ℝ := fun u => 51 / 100 + D.e * grid u
      let height : FreeRow → ℝ := fun u => (3 * idx u + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta
      ‖HighFrontierTargets.normalizedProbeAt F.modulus ⊤ F.S F.exclusions
          F.maximal D.ell 1 2 (fun _ => F.w) F.W F.W
          totalE sourceLx sourceLy eta Z -
        principalPhysicalPool eta F.S T (fun _ y => (F.w y : ℂ)) Y
          F.W F.W (Z ^ sourceLx) (Z ^ sourceLy) Z / normer -
        finiteCentralCubeRows F.S F.exclusions F.maximal eta rows T hT
          (fun _ y => (F.w y : ℂ)) Y F.W F.W
          (Z ^ sourceLx) (Z ^ sourceLy) Z D.e alpha height / normer‖ ≤
        C * Z ^ (HeckeZeroSupremum.beta - 11 / 16 - D.sigma)

/-- A concrete admissible point below `7/8` for which the old small-tail premise fails. -/

    (he : 0<e) (he' : e<1/1000) (hδ : 0<δ) (hδ' : δ≤1/2)
    (ha : 0<a) (hb : 0<b) (hB : 0≤B) (hβ : (7/8:ℝ)≤HeckeZeroSupremum.beta)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (hfirst : FirstTail (1/4) S)
    (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (a0 b0 a1 b1 : ℝ) (ha0 : 0<a0) (ha1 : 0<a1)
    (hW0 : Function.support W0⊆Icc a0 b0) (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Icc a1 b1) :

      (∀n∈F,∀u∈R n,u.val≠1 ∧ (2:ℝ)^n≤((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ) ∧
        ((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ)≤2*(2:ℝ)^n) →
      ∀(T : Fin K→Finset ProbePhysical.PrimeIdeal) (_hT : ∀i P,P∈T i→P.val∉S),

      ≤C*(η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)^δ*Z^(HeckeZeroSupremum.beta-67/99-1/25+8*e)

theorem weighted_principal_product_error_linear_sigma {b : ℝ}
    (hblo : (79/100:ℝ) ≤ b) (hbhi : b ≤ 1) {κ ι : Type*} (S : Finset κ)
    (T : κ → Finset ι) (w Q : κ → ι → ℝ) (A η : κ → ι → ℂ)
    (s : ℂ) (P : ℝ) (hP : 480 ≤ P) (hs : b ≤ s.re)
    (hsmall : 1440 * P ^ (-b) ≤ 1)
    (hw : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, 0 ≤ w j i)
    (hQ : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, P ≤ Q j i)
    (hA : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, ‖A j i‖ ≤ 1)
    (hη : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, ‖η j i‖ = 1)
    (hM : ∀ j ∈ S, 0 < ∑ i ∈ T j, w j i) :
    ‖(∏ j ∈ S, ∑ i ∈ T j, (w j i : ℂ) * principalSlot (Q j i) (A j i) (η j i) s) /
        principalScalar S (fun j => ∑ i ∈ T j, w j i) - 1‖ ≤
      S.card * 2 ^ S.card * (1440 * P ^ (-b))
title: weighted_principal_product_error_linear_sigma

    correctionDefectQuadratic V D v E₁⟩

      errorProductSize u (Finset.univ.image (fun i => (P i).val))) =
      ∏ i, ∑ P : T i, 2880 * ‖weight i P‖ * errorSize u P.val

  let hsp : Supported (Ideal.span {p}) := (span_primaryGenerator_of_supported P.val hs).symm ▸ hs

\begin{remark}[Further improvements]\label{prospect}
A substantially larger perturbation would require estimates that
support the altered lengths:
for example, stronger reflected-row energy or a sharper joint
numerator and error-slot bound, or greater usable capacity in the
inverse and ordinary witness moments. The Euler-region checks,
outer-row bounds, and principal approximation would also have to
remain compatible with that geometry. These estimates have not
been established here for such a change. The present fixed
perturbation provides no automatic iteration to the Riemann
Hypothesis and no guarantee that successive improvements would
reach the critical line. Broader arithmetic questions, including
Hilbert's twelfth problem, are longer-term aspirations for the
program; this argument claims no progress on that problem.
\end{remark}

statement:
#### B2.6.3. Short marked energy without label or puncture

When \(f=r_\rho=1\), every active non-slot prime outside \(R\) divides the powerful part. Thus
\[
2A_0\le O+O(1/\log Z),\qquad 0\le N_0\le A_0.
\]
If \(M+2z\le N_*\), then for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\sum_{0<q_k\ll Z^M}|\mathcal T_d(Z^{N_*};k;V)|^2
\ll_\epsilon
Z^{\,M+(N_*+2z-2M)_+/4+\epsilon}.
\tag{B2.44}
\]
To see this directly from (B2.38), first ignore fixed \(O(1/\log Z)\) errors and choose \(\tau_{\rm ref}\) arbitrarily small. Since
\[
T_d-H\le M+2z-N_*\le0,
\]
retention forces \(\max(H,v+\ell_b)=H+O(\tau_{\rm ref}+1/\log Z)\).
If \(u_h=z_a\), (B2.38) is at most \(M\), up to those errors. Otherwise \(u_h\ge v/2\). Put \(y_d=v+3\ell_b+e_\lambda\); because \(\ell_b\ge0\) and \(e_\lambda\ge-O(1/\log Z)\),
\[
u_h+\ell_b+\frac23e_\lambda
+\frac12(T_d-y_d)_+
\ge \frac14y_d+\frac12(T_d-y_d)_+-O(1/\log Z)
\ge\frac14T_d-O(1/\log Z).
\]
With \(\Delta_H=M-O-H\ge-O(1/\log Z)\), substitution into (B2.38) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
4(E_{\rm ref}-M)
&\le N_*+2z_a-2M-2\Delta_H
-(2A_0-N_0+B_0+4S_0)+O(\tau_{\rm ref}+1/\log Z)\\
&\le N_*+2z-2M+O(\tau_{\rm ref}+1/\log Z).
\end{aligned}
\]
Restoring the row branch, tails, and small-power losses proves (B2.44). No moment estimate or zero-free conclusion enters this proof.
title: B2.6.3. Short marked energy without label or puncture

def ramifiedRegularCoefficients (eta a rho x z : ℂ) (j : ℕ) : QuadraticCoefficients :=
  let Q : ℂ := Ideal.absNorm (Ideal.span {p})
  let V := coordV (Ideal.absNorm (Ideal.span {p})) z
  let X := Q ^ (-x)
  let B := star eta * Q ^ x
  let P₀ := rowClosedMarked p hp hg eta a X 0 V rho j
  let P₁ := rowClosedMarked p hp hg eta a X 1 V rho j - P₀
  let S := B * (1 - V) *
    (rowMarkedTerm p hp hg eta a X 1 V rho j 1 0 1 0 /
      (1 - evenRatio (Ideal.absNorm (Ideal.span {p})) a X V))
  ⟨B * (1 - V) * P₀,
    B * (1 - V) * P₁ - 1 - (1 - V) * P₀ - S,
    -(1 - V) * P₁⟩
title: ramifiedRegularCoefficients

theorem actual_nonfloor_cube_arithmetic (N n : ℕ) (e eps c b A R dmin dmax rmin τ ε κ cost mesh margin loss : ℝ)
    (he : 0 < e) (he1 : e<1/1000) (heps : 0 < eps) (hc : 0 < c) (hcb : c≤b) (hA : 0≤A)
    (hR : 0≤R) (hdmin : 0 < dmin) (hdmax : 0≤dmax) (hdRange : dmin≤dmax) (hrmin : 0 < rmin)
    (hτ : 0<τ) (hε : 0<ε) (hκ : 0<κ) (hcost : 0≤cost) (hmesh : 0 < mesh)
    (hbudget : 8*e*R+κ≤ε) (hgap : ε < rmin*mesh) (hmargin : 0 < margin)
    (hheight : 2*τ < dmin*cost) (hloss : τ*(2+4*eps) < loss)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hfirst : FirstTail (4*e) S)
    (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (ell : Fin N→ℝ) (hell : Function.Injective ell)
    (hello : ∀j,dmax*rmin≤ell j) (hellhi : ∀j,ell j≤dmin*R)
    (W : Fin N→ℝ→ℂ)
    (hWs : ∀j,Function.support (W j)⊆Ioo c b) (hW : ∀j,ContDiff ℝ ∞ (W j)) (hWB : ∀j t,‖W j t‖≤A)
    (hellsum : ∑j,ell j=167/1000)
    (hdtop : dmax≤37/42) (hε1 : ε≤1/1000) (hκ1 : κ≤1)
    (hτzero : τ < dmin/2) (hτheight : 4*τ < dmin*cost)
    (hwbudget : 12*e*((22:ℝ)+2)+8*κ+2*cost≤ε/2)
    (φ : ℝ→ℝ) (hφ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ) (hφc : HasCompactSupport φ)
    (hφp : tsupport φ⊆Ioi 0) (hφ0 : ∀y,0≤φ y) (hφne : φ≠0)
    (a₀ b₀ B₀ : ℝ) (ha₀ : 0 < a₀) (hab₀ : a₀≤b₀) (hB₀ : 0 < B₀)
    (hφs : Function.support φ⊆Ioo a₀ b₀) (hφB : ∀y,φ y≤B₀)
    (εm ν logCost heightCost momentCost : ℝ)
    (hεm : 0<εm) (hν : 0<ν)
    (hlog : 0 < logCost) (hMomentHeight : τ < heightCost)
    (μ : ℝ)
    (hfinal : (159*ε+εm+R+7*ν)+(12*e+eps*(N+8))+
      (logCost+heightCost+momentCost+loss+mesh*167/1000+(13243/1000)*e)+μ≤1/40000) (counts : CountParameters M H εm) :
    ∃C : ℝ,0 < C ∧
    ∀η : Character,∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,
      ∀d : ℝ,dmin≤d → d≤dmax → ∀(v a C0 : ℝ),0≤v → v≤d → d-v≤μ →
      51/100 < a → a≤7/8 → WeightedQRH.OriginalBranch d a → 0≤C0 → ∀rows : Finset FreeRow,
      (∀u∈rows,u.val≠1 ∧ Z^(1/100:ℝ)≤rowNorm u ∧
        (calibrationForSet S hmax).residueMonoid u.val≠0 ∧ rowNorm u≤Z^(d-margin)) →
      (∀u∈rows,Z^v≤rowNorm u ∧ rowNorm u≤2*Z^v) →
      ∀i : ℕ,i≤n →
      (∀u∈rows,detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily S hS.prime η u (rayCubeFamily M H hH u))
        (3*(i+1:ℕ)*Z^τ) < a+2*e) →
      (∀u∈rows,a≤detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily S hS.prime η u (rayCubeFamily M H hH u))
        ((3*i:ℕ)*Z^τ)) →
      let Y : Fin N→ℝ

theorem continued_source_eq_raw {ι : Type*} (η : Character) (S : Finset Id)
    (hS : ∀ P ∈ S, Prime P) (J : Finset ι) (T : ι → Finset PrimeIdeal)
    (b : ι → PrimeIdeal → ℂ) (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (X Y Z : ℝ) (x w z : ℂ)
    (hx0 : x≠0) (hx1 : x≠1) :
    continuedSourceMultiplier η S hS J T b W0 W1 X Y Z x w z =
      sourceMultiplier W0 W1 X Y Z (η.excludePrimes S hS) x
        (globalClosedCorrection η S x) (slotMultiplier η J T b x) w z

statement:
# The quartic QRH boundary

Hailey Collet · HaileyCollet@gmail.com · Apache-2.0  
Proof ID: `cycle25-quartic-20261010` · Catalogue status: **verification-pending**

This submission proves nonvanishing in the open half-plane `Re(s) > b₀`, where

\[
b_0=\frac{11}{12}-\frac{\ell_0}{4},\qquad
927\ell_0^4-3135\ell_0^3+2433\ell_0^2+275\ell_0-100=0,
\]

and `ℓ₀` is the unique root in `[1/6, 1/5]`. Lean also certifies the tighter isolating interval `0.16712007850680 < ℓ₀ < 0.16712007850682`. The rational catalogue bound is

\[
\theta=\frac{683505193}{781250000}=0.87488664704,
\qquad 0<\theta-b_0<4\times10^{-14}.
\]

The theorem covers Mathlib's Riemann zeta function, every complex Dirichlet character of every positive modulus, and OpenAI's finite-order Hecke family over `ℚ(ζ₃)`. The Dirichlet and Hecke statements retain their principal-character pole exceptions. The zeta endpoint uses Mathlib's totalized definition; the usual analytic reading excludes `s = 1`. Nothing here asserts a result for Hecke characters over other number fields. All claimed half-planes are strict.

The public entrypoint is `formalization/Cycle25/Assembly/Final/Endpoint.lean`. It exports `Cycle25.beta_le_theta`, `Cycle25.hecke_nonzero`, `Cycle25.dirichlet_nonzero` and `Cycle25.zeta_nonzero` at the exact boundary. The `*_catalogue` versions use the rational bound above. Despite its name, `Cycle25.theta` denotes the exact boundary; `Cycle25.Arithmetic.theta` denotes the rational rounding.

The proof combines variable-κ moments, reflected physical numerator estimates and a common-probe contradiction. It reuses OpenAI's coarse `7/8` bound to initialize the argument, Akash Levy's weighted-numerator construction, and the completed zero-slot moment from the earlier `4/33` branch. These dependencies are part of the proof. The final nonvanishing declarations require no supplied analytic estimate.

There is also a reusable auxiliary result in `formalization/Cycle25/Energy/Endpoint.lean`: `Cycle25.Energy.terminal_positive_at`. It treats the original canonical ray-prime family with one common smooth slot profile, `7/10 ≤ κ ≤ 3/4`, `β ≥ 51/100` and `2β − 1 ≤ κ`. It preserves the original `NaturalState` eligibility and `PositiveAt` conclusion. Its mesh depends on the cap, mask, profile-control parameters and ε, with seminorm orders chosen before the character and ideal and constants chosen afterward. The precise smoothness, support and arithmetic conditions are in the declaration. This result can be used through that interface without assuming the new quartic nonvanishing conclusion.

Lean, NanoDa and con-ron accepted all seven exported statements and their proof closures, with exact-statement comparison and only the three standard axioms. The clean source rebuild also passed: 301 modules compiled against pinned upstream libraries. See [Verification.md](Verification.md) for the scope, controls and recorded results. All three kernels passed; acceptance as **framework-verified** is requested. Catalogue status remains **verification-pending** until maintainer review. See `REPRODUCE.md` for reproduction and evidence, and [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) for authorship and source attribution.

      ‖finiteCentralCubeRows S hS hmax η (cubeBinRows (rows ∩ dyadicRows 1 k) idx grid i j)

def SourceMomentBoundAt {N : ℕ}
    (M : Ideal O) [NeZero M] [Finite (O ⧸ M)]
    (H : Subgroup (O ⧸ M)ˣ) (hH : RayOrthogonality.globalUnits M ≤ H)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S)
    (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal) (ell : Fin N → ℝ) (W : Fin N → ℝ → ℝ)
    (dmin dmax b epsilon rowMargin slotMesh binWidth gamma epsilonM : ℝ)
    (counts : CountParameters M H epsilonM) (η : Character)
    (Z theta C height : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀rows : Finset HeckeInverseAmplification.FreeRow, ∀d a : ℝ,
    dmin ≤ d → d ≤ dmax → (51/100 : ℝ) < a → a ≤ 1 →
    (∀u∈rows,u.val ≠ 1 ∧ Z ^ (1/100 : ℝ) ≤ rowNorm u ∧
      (calibrationForSet S hmax).residueMonoid u.val ≠ 0 ∧
      rowNorm u ≤ Z ^ (d - rowMargin)) →
    ∀i : ℕ, ∀z : ℂ, z.re = 17/50 → |z.im| ≤ height →
    SourceMomentsAt M H hH S hS.prime η rows ell (fun j y => (W j y : ℂ))
      Z d a epsilon theta dmax b slotMesh binWidth i z gamma
      (if 2*a-1 ≤ 5/6 then counts.cB else counts.cH)
      (if 2*a-1 ≤ 5/6 then counts.kB else counts.kH) C height epsilonM

statement:
\begin{proposition}[Arithmetic package]\label{prop:arithmetic}
The general reflected-energy estimate \eqref{eq:full-energy-proved},
the Gram estimate \eqref{eq:Gram-proved}, the marked inverse
moment of Lemma~\ref{lem:marked}, and its sixth-power amplification
in Appendix~\ref{app:inverse} hold with the coefficient and zero
conventions specified in their proofs.  They are unconditional.
The plain moment of Lemma~\ref{lem:plain} holds on
\(13/18\le\kappa\le1\), under \(B\le(1+\kappa)/2\) for
positive slots when \(\kappa<1\), and without that premise at
\(\kappa=1\) or in the zero-slot case.
Its mesh is independent of the fixed arithmetic datum and fixed
slot count.  Each estimate has finite-seminorm and fixed-polynomial
height uniformity on bounded length ranges.
\end{proposition}
title: prop:arithmetic

theorem actual_floor_cube_arithmetic_totalE
    (N n : ℕ) (e eps c b A R dmin dmax rmin tau epsilon kappa cost mesh delta margin loss : ℝ)
    (he : 0 < e) (he1 : e < 1 / 1000) (heps : 0 < eps)
    (hc : 0 < c) (hcb : c ≤ b) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hR : 0 ≤ R)
    (hdmin : 0 < dmin) (hdmax : 0 ≤ dmax) (hdRange : dmin ≤ dmax)
    (hrmin : 0 < rmin) (htau : 0 < tau) (hepsilon : 0 < epsilon)
    (hkappa : 0 < kappa) (hcost : 0 ≤ cost) (hmesh : 0 < mesh)
    (hdelta : 0 < delta) (hbudget : 8 * e * R + kappa ≤ epsilon)
    (hgap : epsilon < rmin * mesh) (hmargin : 0 < margin)
    (hheight : 2 * tau < dmin * cost) (hloss : tau * (2 + 4 * eps) < loss)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S)
    (hfirst : FirstTail (4 * e) S) (hmax : ∀P∈S, P.IsMaximal)
    (ell : Fin N → ℝ) (hell : Function.Injective ell)
    (hello : ∀j, dmax * rmin ≤ ell j) (hellhi : ∀j, ell j ≤ dmin * R)
    (W : Fin N → ℝ → ℂ)
    (hWs : ∀j, Function.support (W j) ⊆ Ioo c b)
    (hW : ∀j, ContDiff ℝ ∞ (W j)) (hWB : ∀j t, ‖W j t‖ ≤ A)
    (hellsum : ∑j, ell j = totalE) :
    ∃C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀eta : Character, ∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,
      ∀d : ℝ, dmin ≤ d → d ≤ dmax → ∀v : ℝ, 0 ≤ v →
      ∀rows : Finset FreeRow,
      (∀u∈rows, u.val ≠ 1 ∧ Z ^ delta ≤ rowNorm u ∧
        (calibrationForSet S hmax).residueMonoid u.val ≠ 0 ∧
        rowNorm u ≤ Z ^ (d - margin)) →
      (∀u∈rows, Z ^ v ≤ rowNorm u ∧ rowNorm u ≤ 2 * Z ^ v) →
      ∀i : ℕ, i ≤ n →
      (∀u∈rows, detectorMaximum
        (sourceDetectorFamily S hS.prime eta u (rayCubeFamily M H hH u))
        (3 * (i + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ tau) < 51 / 100 + 2 * e) →
      let Y : Fin N → ℝ

theorem weighted_principal_product_error {κ ι : Type*} (S : Finset κ)
    (T : κ → Finset ι) (w Q : κ → ι → ℝ) (A η : κ → ι → ℂ)
    (s : ℂ) (P : ℝ) (hP : 480 ≤ P) (hs : 87/100 ≤ s.re)
    (hw : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, 0 ≤ w j i)
    (hQ : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, P ≤ Q j i)
    (hA : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, ‖A j i‖ ≤ 1)
    (hη : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ i ∈ T j, ‖η j i‖ = 1)
    (hM : ∀ j ∈ S, 0 < ∑ i ∈ T j, w j i) :
    ‖(∏ j ∈ S, ∑ i ∈ T j, (w j i : ℂ) * principalSlot (Q j i) (A j i) (η j i) s) /
        principalScalar S (fun j => ∑ i ∈ T j, w j i) - 1‖ ≤
      (1 + 1440 * P ^ (-(87/100 : ℝ))) ^ S.card - 1

statement:
### C.2. Canonical estimate and cube completion

We claim that, for every fixed \(C_0\ge1,\kappa>0\),
\[
E(H,X,F;\xi,W)\ll Z^\varepsilon\Sigma\|W\|_{C^J}^2,
\quad \Sigma=XF\le Z^{C_0},\quad
H,X,F\ge1,\quad H\le\Sigma Z^{-\kappa}.
\tag{C.5}
\]
The derivative order is independent of the location of the fixed support interval.

For \(\Psi_{k,f}(n)=\xi(n)\chi_n(k)\chi_n(f)^4\), cube inversion gives the exact identity
\[
X^{-1/2}\sum_n^{*}a_\xi(n)\chi_n(k)\chi_n(f)^4W(q_n/X)
=\sum_h\frac{\mu(h)\overline{\alpha(h)}^{3}\Psi_{k,f}(h)^3}{q_h}
T(X/q_h^3;k,f).
\tag{C.6}
\]
After opening \(T\), the coefficient of each total cube \(b\) contains \(\sum_{h\mid b}\mu(h)\), so only \(b=1\) survives. Complete multiplicativity with zeros is essential here.

Put \(H_c^3=\min(X,X^2/H^2)\), \(L_b=X/q_b^3\). Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and (B.13) bound the terms \(q_h\le H_c\), after averaging \(f\), by
\[
Z^\varepsilon\|W\|_{C^J}^2\left(H+\frac{H^2F H_c^3}{X}\right)
\ll Z^\varepsilon\Sigma\|W\|_{C^J}^2\quad(H\le\Sigma).
\]
Reopen \(T\) in the remaining terms. The coefficient of a total cube is
\(\overline{\alpha(b)}^{3}\xi(b)^3 1_{(b,f)=1}\sum_{h\mid b,q_h>H_c}\mu(h)\), of modulus at most \(\tau(b)\); \(\chi_b(k)^3\) is a bounded row multiplier. Since \(\sum_{q_b\le R}\tau(b)/q_b\ll\log^2(2R)\), a second weighted Cauchy–Schwarz yields
\[
E(H,X,F;\xi,W)
\ll Z^\varepsilon\left\{\Sigma\|W\|_{C^J}^2+
\sup_{q_b>H_c,\ L_b>1}E(H,L_b,F;\xi,W)\right\}.
\tag{C.7}
\]
For \(L_b\le1\), a nonempty annular support contains only boundedly many columns and costs \(O(H)\). In particular, the supremum is empty if \(H^2\le X\).
title: C.2. Canonical estimate and cube completion

  ∀q : ℝ,∀B : Batch M H (Sum Bool (RayQuotient.Characters M H)) (Fin N)

    (∀u∈B.rows,∀j,B.family u j=sourceDetectorFamily S hS η u (rayCubeFamily M H hH u) j) →
    ∀bin j J K,∀hne : (B.fiberRows bin j J K).Nonempty,

statement:
### 2.3. The local compensation and its bounds

At a selected prime of norm \(Q\), use \(V=Q^{-6z}\), \(W=\psi_u(\mathfrak p)Q^{-w}\), and \(D=\eta(\mathfrak p)\overline{\psi_u(\mathfrak p)}Q^{-s}\), as in the local table (A.8)–(A.9). Set \(c_{\mathfrak p}=\overline{\eta(\mathfrak p)}Q^s\), \(h_{\mathfrak p}=Q^{-w}\), and
\[
 G_{\mathfrak p}=
 \frac{(c_{\mathfrak p}-h_{\mathfrak p})(1-V)(1-W)P_{\mathfrak p}^*
       -h_{\mathfrak p}(1-VW)}{1-D}.
\tag{2.9}
\]
Direct substitution gives
\[
 \overline{\eta(\mathfrak p)}Q^{s+z-1}P_{\mathfrak p}^*-Q^{z-w-1}P_{\mathfrak p}
 =\frac{1-D}{(1-V)(1-W)}Q^{z-1}G_{\mathfrak p}.
\tag{2.10}
\]
Thus (2.5) has representation (2.8) with \(H_{\eta,u}\) replaced by
\[
 \mathcal H_{\eta,u,Z}=
 \sum_{\mathfrak p\notin S}w(Q/P)Q^{z-1}G_{\mathfrak p}
 \prod_{\mathfrak q\ne\mathfrak p,\ \mathfrak q\notin S}H_{\mathfrak q}.
\tag{2.11}
\]
This formula does not divide by an Euler correction. If \(\mathfrak p\nmid u\), put \(v=\chi_{\mathfrak p}(u)\) and \(E_{\mathfrak p}=P_{\mathfrak p}^*+D\). Since \(c_{\mathfrak p}D=v^{-1}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 G_{\mathfrak p}+v^{-1}H_{\mathfrak p}
 =\frac{(1-V)(1-W)}{1-D}\bigg[&(v^{-1}-h_{\mathfrak p})
 \left(\frac V{1-V}-D\right)\\
 &+(c_{\mathfrak p}+v^{-1}-h_{\mathfrak p})E_{\mathfrak p}\bigg].
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.12}
\]
The leading selected-prime character is therefore \(-\overline{\psi_u(\mathfrak p)}\).

The local table has two useful domains:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 \mathcal B:&\Re s\ge51/100,\quad\Re z\ge17/50,\quad\Re w\ge-1/100,
                  \quad\Re(s+w)\ge1+\epsilon_1;\\
 \mathcal B_1:&\Re s\ge87/100,\quad\Re w\ge3/4,\quad\Re z\ge1/8.
\end{array}
\tag{2.13}
\]
On compact real boxes in \(\mathcal B\), \(H_{\eta,u}\) is holomorphic and \(\ll q_u^\varepsilon\), uniformly in heights. The leading unramified defects have sizes \(Q^{-s-w}\) and \(Q^{4-6s-6z}\), at most \(Q^{-1-\epsilon_1}\) and \(Q^{-11/10}\); every other term has a summable fixed margin. At primes of \(u\), the defects have negative exponents and their finite product costs \(q_u^\varepsilon\). On \(\mathcal B_1\), the principal-row defects are \(O(Q^{-137/100})\); (2.12) gives a selected-prime error \(O(Q^{-1/2})\). These estimates follow after canceling the apparent \(1-W\) denominator in the table, so no pole at that factor is introduced.

For later use put \(z_0=17/50\). On the central lines
\[
 \Re s=a+16e,\qquad \Re w=1-a-6e,\qquad \Re z=z_0,
 \qquad 51/100\le a\le11/12,
\tag{2.14}
\]
choose the cutoff in \(S\) so that \(|H_{\mathfrak p}-1|<1/2\). Only on these lines write
\[
 \mathcal H_{\eta,u,Z}=H_{\eta,u}(\mathcal Q+\mathcal D),\qquad
 \mathcal Q=-\sum_{\mathfrak p}w(Q/P)Q^{z-1}\overline{\psi_u(\mathfrak p)},
\quad
 \mathcal D=\sum_{\mathfrak p}w(Q/P)Q^{z-1}\frac{G_{\mathfrak p}}{H_{\mathfrak p}}-\mathcal Q.
\tag{2.15}
\]
The reciprocal contours used to bound these factors will be supplied in §3.

**Lemma 2.1 (ramified error).** If the reflected primitive numerator has a subpower conductor-height bound in the row's buffered zero-free region, then, for \(q_u\asymp U\),
\[
 |L_K^S(w,\psi_u)\mathcal D|
 \ll U^{a-1/2+O(e)+\varepsilon}(1+T)^A P^{z_0-1/2+O(e)+\varepsilon}.
\tag{2.16}
\]
**Proof.** Off \(u\), (2.12) gives an error \(O(Q^{-51/100})\), which is stronger after prime summation. At row valuation \(j>0\), the non-tail terms, after removing \(Q^{z_0}\), have boundary exponents
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
 j&1&2&3&4&5\\ \hline
 &a-2&1/2-2a&-a,\ 1-3a&1/2-2a&2-5a.
\end{array}
\]
All are less than \(-1/2\). The geometric tails preserve this bound, except for the term of size \(Q^{z_0-\Re w}\) at \(j\ge2\). Here the primitive numerator conductor is \(\ll_S UQ^{-(j-1)}\), because its good conductor exponent is one. With \(A_*=1/2-\Re w=a-1/2+6e\), reflection bounds this summand together with the numerator by
\[
 U^{A_*+\varepsilon}(1+T)^A
 Q^{z_0-\Re w-(j-1)A_*}
 \le U^{A_*+\varepsilon}(1+T)^A Q^{z_0-1/2}.
\]
The equality \(-\Re w-A_*=-1/2\) supplies the saving. Sum the divisor-many primes dividing \(u\); their original zeros require no Euler restoration. ∎

The quotient-free formula also gives
\[
 \mathcal H_{\eta,u,Z}\ll U^\varepsilon
 \begin{cases}
 Z^{\ell z_0},&(\Re s,\Re w,\Re z)=(\beta_*+e,1/2,z_0),\\
 Z^{\ell v},&(\Re s,\Re w,\Re z)=(2,2,v),\quad v>2,
 \end{cases}
\tag{2.17}
\]
when \(\beta_*>29/33\). On the first line the selected factors are \(O(1)\) off \(u\) and \(O(Q^{1/2})\) on its divisor-many primes; on the second they are \(O(1)\). The unselected product has the same convergent majorant. On all intervening fixed boxes the full correction has size \(U^\varepsilon Z^B\), for a fixed \(B\) chosen before tail orders.
title: 2.3. The local compensation and its bounds

private def planDependencyPatch (root : FilePath) (dependency : Dependency) : IO PatchPlan := do
  let label := dependency.dirName
  let some (.git url (some revision) none) := dependency.src?
    | throw <| IO.userError s!"{label}: compatibility patches require a Git dependency pinned to a commit."
  unless revision.length == 40 && revision.toList.all (fun c =>
      c.isDigit || ('a' <= c && c <= 'f')) do
    throw <| IO.userError s!"{label}: expected a full lowercase Git commit, got {revision}."
  let patch := root / "patches" / s!"{label}-lean4341.patch"
  unless ← patch.pathExists do
    throw <| IO.userError s!"Missing compatibility patch: {patch}"
  let directory := root / ".lake" / "packages" / label
  let plan := { label, directory, patch, url, revision, state := .absent : PatchPlan }
  unless ← directory.pathExists do
    return plan
  let head ← patchGit directory #["rev-parse", "HEAD"]
  unless head.exitCode == 0 && head.stdout.trimAscii.toString == revision do
    throw <| IO.userError s!"{label}: expected commit {revision}, got {head.stdout}\n{head.stderr}"
  let origin ← patchGit directory #["remote", "get-url", "origin"]
  unless origin.exitCode == 0 && origin.stdout.trimAscii.toString == url do
    throw <| IO.userError s!"{label}: expected origin {url}, got {origin.stdout}\n{origin.stderr}"
  let reverse ← checkPatch directory patch #["--reverse"]
  if reverse.exitCode == 0 then
    return {plan with state := .applied}
  let forward ← checkPatch directory patch
  if forward.exitCode == 0 then
    return {plan with state := .needsApply}
  throw <| IO.userError s!"{label}: compatibility patch conflicts with local changes.\n\
    Forward check:\n{forward.stderr}\nReverse check:\n{reverse.stderr}"
